subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Fire towers send out crucial early warnings to help detect wildfires before they spread.
• Before aerial surveillance, fire towers were staffed by fire tower observers.
• Dorothy Jensen was the fire tower observer at Palisade Peak Tower in Colorado.
• She held this position for twenty-one years (1932-1953).
• Margaret Walsh was the fire tower observer at Mount Sterling Tower in North Carolina.
• She held this position for fifty-two years (1898-1950).
prompt: The student wants to compare the length of time Dorothy Jensen and Margaret Walsh worked as fire tower observers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Dorothy Jensen worked as a fire tower observer for twenty-one years, but Margaret Walsh did so for even longer: fifty-two years.
choices.B: From 1932 to 1953, the forests of Colorado were safer thanks to fire tower observers Dorothy Jensen and Margaret Walsh.
choices.C: Dorothy Jensen and Margaret Walsh were both fire tower observers at a time when such a person was needed to staff a fire tower.
choices.D: Before aerial surveillance, fire tower observers like Dorothy Jensen, who served for twenty-one years, and Margaret Walsh were crucial to detecting wildfires early.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it directly accomplishes the goal of comparing the lengths of service for both fire tower observers. The sentence provides Jensen's duration (twenty-one years) and Walsh's duration (fifty-two years), and uses the comparative phrase 'even longer' to explicitly establish that Walsh served for a greater length of time. This structure allows readers to immediately understand both the specific durations and the comparative relationship between them, fully satisfying the student's stated rhetorical purpose.
